additional_concerns: Candidates node.1bf6918f69c6b37738daeb83, node.4e6a162c35678e9ddf17ad8e, node.ce439b1cf9ed8301fbb68f94 and node.ea4d19630f8cab09065b1909 turn preserved processing of existing applications into a substantive relief exclusion. The source establishes continued processing but does not expressly establish that broader consequence or its duration. Their formulas preserve a proposed interpretation, not a settled source rule.

Candidate node.4d548f2e09bc36ef51212f64 excludes legacy applications from its question and scope. That restriction leaves their treatment unanswered; it does not establish their substantive disqualification.

Candidate node.8eb374ffa546ddd2ba291e37 supplies no executable formalization. Its unresolved actual-relief question cannot yield an executable eligibility conclusion. Candidate node.b66b3e831bb98a12db59dffa instead answers only the substantive conditions and cannot establish actual procedural availability.

The introductory immediate-effect language and the explicit 28 November 2025 commencement provision must be read together. The latter supports the specified commencement date, but the supplied text does not settle every legally relevant assessment or implementation event.

The relevant updated FAQs, including the FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds, are missing and are needed to resolve detailed transition and procedural availability questions. No supplied dependency metadata identifies which opaque missing dependency ID denotes those FAQs; no catalogue match can be inferred. Applicable home-jurisdiction requirements and authoritative guidance on novel or complex features and local policy implications are also absent for concrete classification.

The home-supervision aim supports context, not an express additional item (ii) eligibility condition. A broader scope interpretation remains possible, but neither imposing a separate supervision predicate nor declaring it categorically irrelevant to all interpretation is established here.

All executable candidates rely on supplied legal classifications. Their Boolean formulas do not determine home compliance, materiality, product novelty or complexity, or possible local policy implications. These checks do not validate those classifications or establish the complete underlying approval obligation.
